neighbours.label: modal or verb of a clause saying what the speaker/agent will do with a just-mentioned thing (so I can V it, to V it, and I will V it)
fire: Pass me the photograph so I can show it to your grandmother.
Leave the bicycle by the door so that I may repair it in the morning.
Email me the contract and I will review it before lunch.
The vet took a little blood from the dog to test it for parasites.
Give us the address so we can deliver it this afternoon.
Put the kettle on the table so I can fill it for you.
Bring your essay on Friday and I will mark it over the weekend.
The mechanic lifted the engine out to inspect it for cracks.
quiet: My grandmother can see the photograph from her chair.
The bicycle by the door may need a new chain.
The contract will expire before the end of the year.
The vet said the dog was free of parasites.
We can find the address on the back of the envelope.
The kettle on the table can hold two litres.
Your essay on Friday was the best in the class.
The mechanic said the engine had no cracks.

short: so I can V it (purpose clause)
notes: Card: ' tell', ' examine', ' give', ' send', ' could', ' will' in purpose clauses ('so I can tell you', 'to examine it'), also Spanish/Arabic subjunctives. Probes: 'so I can read it' 0.96, 'so that I may bless them' 0.84, 'and I will check it' 0.72, 'to test it' 0.49; 'He can read the letter' 0.01, 'wants to read the letter' 0.03, 'to ask him' 0.07.
